correctness.rationale: Under finite irreducibility and the independent iid positive-integer finite-mean clock, occupation includes ages 0 through L−1, not the pre-reset endpoint. Renewal reward and telescoping give μp(I−P)=e_v−E[e_vP^L]. The right side has TV norm q because its positive part is concentrated at v. Thus dTV(p,pP)=q/μ; invariance of π and TV contraction give dTV(p,pP)≤2dTV(p,π). On a star from its hub, even ages are at the hub and odd ages are uniform on leaves. The excess hub mass is Pr(L odd)/(2μ), all leaf deviations have the opposite sign, and q=Pr(L odd). This proves equality for any clock there, with positive q possible. The flux vanishes iff q=0, and irreducibility then makes p=π. Nonnegative mismatch for each supported length forces exact return at each of those lengths. For any one exact-return length ℓ, d divides ℓ, and all iterates jℓ are exact returns; the periodic limit is dπ_v. The cyclic class has total π mass 1/d with strictly positive masses, so it is the singleton {v}. Conversely a singleton class is visited with certainty at all period multiples. In a connected loopless simple undirected walk with at least two states, a singleton cyclic class requires bipartiteness with a singleton side, hence a hub-centered star, and the clock must be even. No fixed-time phase convergence is used. Exact-rational corroboration for a mixed clock on a star and two clocks on a directed 3-cycle is recorded at /workspace/branches/cf7431a9-1fde-40f3-9347-5db1a19d1c30/independent_replay.txt. The supplied check.py was inspected, not executed. See RESULT.md lines 17–65 for conventions, proof and reported finite checks.

The distinct finding supported by the comparison is the sharp imbalance estimate in the actual pre-reset mismatch, together with the necessary-and-sufficient structural criterion for invisibility over all independent renewal clocks. No matched theorem states or entails that full classification and sharp application on the evidence checked. This is a best-of-knowledge finding with limited primary-text access.

value.rationale: The mismatch probability is an observable of individual reset excursions, yet it gives a universally sharp quantitative lower bound on the static occupation bias. The qualitative side resolves when a nonzero schedule can leave the occupation unchanged: it is not merely cancellation in the average, but almost-sure invisible resets with a rigid graph/clock classification. The exact condition and sharp example give usable content beyond the routine norm bound alone.
